about: The vocabulary and the decision table that turn several sources into one screening class per 1 km block. blocks.py reads its thresholds and rules from this file, and the app draws its evidence graph from it, so the code, the documentation and the picture cannot drift apart. Version 2 was rewritten after an independent audit: class names now say what was seen, not what to do about it.

object_types.Source: A dataset from one instrument or one mapping effort.
object_types.Block: A 1 km square of ground inside a site.
object_types.Observation: One number about a block, taken from one source.
object_types.State: A yes or no statement about a block, decided by a rule over observations.
object_types.Action: A screening class: what was seen on the block and what a field team could check there. It is not a recommendation to intervene.

thresholds.note: These are choices made on 14 Nov 2026, the day of the first results, and not derived from a reference. docs/LIMITS.md shows how the counts move when each one moves.

states.title: On mapped peat
states.why: The classes are given on mapped peat only. PEATMAP here is the national peat mapping; it has its own errors.

states.title: HH fell on both orbits
states.why: Over open and thinly vegetated land, L-band HH falls as the surface dries. It also changes with clearing, harvest and standing water, which this rule cannot tell apart. Two orbits that look from opposite sides must both see the fall, which shows it is on the ground and not in one orbit.

states.title: Fire detected
states.why: A thermal detection from another instrument. It marks active fire seen from space, with pixels of 0.4 to 1 km or more, and misses some fire under smoke. It is not a burnt-area map.

states.title: Still low after the first rain
states.why: On the first pass after the rain, HH was still at least half a decibel below its dry-start level on both orbits. This rests on one pass per orbit taken within days of heavy rain, and we do not know why some land stayed low.

states.title: HV low after the rain
states.rule: fire and hv_left_asc >= hv_left_db and hv_left_desc >= hv_left_db
states.why: HV comes mostly from woody vegetation. After the rain, HV on peat with fire detections sat about half a decibel below peat without them, on both orbits. HV is used as measured, without the forest baseline.

states.title: Fire on several days
states.why: Detections on three or more separate days at one spot, which a single false detection cannot produce.

states.title: No fire detected within 1 km
states.why: The cautious reading of no fire nearby: nothing detected within 1 km of any part of the block.

states.title: Near a mapped canal
states.why: Shown for context only and not used in any class. In our data the fall in HH does not change with distance to a mapped canal, and OpenStreetMap is incomplete here.

actions.title: Fire detected on peat
actions.advice: Fire was detected on this peat during the season. A place to check for burn damage and lost vegetation.

actions.title: Fell, and still low after the rain
actions.rule: on_peat and fell and not fire and still_low
actions.advice: The radar echo fell on both orbits, no fire was detected on the block, and it was still low on the first pass after the rain. Worth a field check: we do not know why it stayed low.

actions.title: Fell, and came back with the rain
actions.rule: on_peat and fell and not fire and not still_low
actions.advice: The radar echo fell on both orbits, no fire was detected on the block, and it was back near its dry-start level on the first pass after the rain.

actions.title: No class
actions.advice: The echo did not fall by 1 dB on both orbits, or the block is outside mapped peat. Fire outside peat is still shown on the map.

confidence.label: Agreement
confidence.rule: A count, not a probability. One point when the class's own rule holds, plus one for each further condition in its stronger_if list that also holds. Three or more is high, two is medium, one is low.

caveat: A screening result from one season with no ground measurements. It shows where the radar echo changed and where fire was detected, and where a field visit would be most informative. It does not measure the water table and does not recommend an intervention.
